category_title: Year 9 boys with SEBD who resist modified games and technical practice
minimal_context: The student is participating in a Year 9 Physical Education class where the goal is to complete a peer assessment task identifying a partner's strengths and weaknesses.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: For this next activity, I need you to work with your partner and identify their personal strengths and weaknesses from the game.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Wanders away from his partner) I'm not doing this paired stuff.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please go back to your partner and try the assessment.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Walks back over) Fine. Your weakness is that you're completely useless at passing.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What do you think would be a better way to say that?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: No, it's true, he's an idiot! (Starts arguing aggressively with the partner) You can't even kick the ball straight, you're terrible!

task.content: identify personal strengths and weaknesses of their peers

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When pupils were asked to identify personal strengths and weaknesses of their peers
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: they were often negative and critical of each other
